title: SystemSketch — Workspace sort UI directions
brief: Five compact ways to change the file organizer from name ordering to newest modified first. The shared fixture is Projects with two folders and three documents, so the placement and mental model—not sample content—drive the choice.
defaultWhy: V1 puts the exact control Zach described directly above the file-name column, keeps the current order legible, and adds no extra browsing surface.
decisionHinge: If visible timestamps matter more than the direct above-column target, V5's metadata column can overtake V1; if future sort modes are imminent, V3 earns its added indirection.
invariants: The same folders and three documents appear in every direction.
Folders stay grouped before documents in both sort states.
A labelled, keyboard-reachable action makes the active sort observable.
boundary: Prototype only — these are live HTML interaction slices inside a comparison gallery. They exercise state change and layout, not the production React dialog or persisted sort preference.

requirements.name: Sort target is discoverable at the file list
requirements.why: The user specifically wants a click target directly above the column, so the control should be found where the ordering is read.
requirements.passCondition: A person opening the list can identify how to switch to recently modified files without scanning unrelated dialog chrome.

anchors.1: The control is hidden or requires a separate conceptual step.
anchors.3: The control is visible but not closely tied to the rows it changes.
anchors.5: The control is immediately visible at the affected column or list edge.

requirements.name: Recent work is quick to scan
requirements.why: The feature exists so a returning user can find what they touched most recently, not merely change a preference.
requirements.passCondition: The prototype visibly puts Gripper, then Legacy, then Arm after recent order is selected.

anchors.3: Newest-first order is present but the active meaning needs interpretation.
anchors.5: Order, direction, and relative age are all legible in one glance.

requirements.name: The organizer stays simple and compact
requirements.why: This should be a small upgrade to an existing file dialog, not a new browser workflow.
requirements.passCondition: The shared two-pane organizer remains recognizably compact and folders remain grouped first.

anchors.1: The solution consumes too much dialog space or changes the organizer's role.
anchors.3: It works but adds an avoidable new surface or explanation burden.
anchors.5: It feels like a natural part of the existing file list with almost no extra chrome.

hardGates.name: Folders stay grouped first
hardGates.why: Sorting recent documents must not bury navigation folders among files.

hardGates.name: The primary state change is a real labelled control
hardGates.why: A visual mock alone cannot establish that the compact interaction is judgeable.

variants.name: Column header
variants.thesis: A clickable Name / Last modified header owns the action directly above the file names.
variants.bestWhen: You want the action anchored exactly where the ordering is read, especially in a dense list.
variants.losesWhen: You need timestamps to be the dominant information or expect many future sorting modes.

decisions.label: Control owner
decisions.value: The primary Name header is the toggle.

decisions.label: Feedback
decisions.value: The header label and downward arrow become Last modified ↓.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.value: The action remains fixed above the rows.

proof: The direct control changes the same shared three-document ordering from name to newest first.
The miniature holds folders above documents before and after sorting.

steps.label: Read the default
steps.caption: Name is the default and the header itself advertises that relationship.

steps.label: Switch to recent
steps.caption: Last modified ↓ is now the header and the documents move newest first.

variants.losesWhen: The immediate one-click recent-files task is more important than a future settings surface.
